title_ar: الإيمان قبل العلم وما يستحيل في حق الله تعالى
title_en: Faith Before Knowledge, and What Is Rationally Impossible of God
body_ar:
لله تعالى الأسماء الحسنى والصفات العلا، وقد قسم العلماء ما يتعلق بالله من الصفات إلى مستحيلة وواجبة وجائزة بحسب أقسام الحكم العقلي، وفي هذه المادة يشرح الشيخ هذا التقسيم، وما يترتب عليه من الكلام.
أقسام الحكم العقلي وتعلق الصفات بها:
الحمد لله رب العالمين، والصلاة والسلام على رسوله محمد، وعلى آله وصحبه أجمعين. وبعد: فهنا يلزمنا أن نعرف أن الحكم العقلي ثلاثة أقسام هي: - الوجوب. - والاستحالة. - والجواز. فالوجوب هو: أن يحكم العقل بثبوت شيء بحيث لا يقبل ارتفاعه. والاستحالة هي: أن يحكم العقل بنفي شيء بحيث لا يقبل ثبوته. والجواز هو: أن يحكم العقل بتساوي الأمرين بحيث يجوز نفي هذا وإثباته. ومجال صفات الله سبحانه وتعالى أحكام العقل ثلاثة كذلك: النوع الأول من الصفات ما يوجبه العقل لله بها، وهذا فيه الصفات المذكورة، حيث يوجبها العقل السليم ودل عليها النقل الصحيح...
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* To God, exalted is He, belong the most beautiful names and the most exalted attributes. The scholars have divided what pertains to God of attributes into the rationally impossible, the necessary and the possible, according to the divisions of the rational judgement; and in this material the Sheikh explains this division and what follows from it in the science of theology (kalām).

## The divisions of the rational judgement, and how the attributes relate to them

Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds, and blessing and peace upon His Messenger Muhammad and upon his family and his Companions all together. And now: here it is necessary for us to know that the rational judgement falls into three divisions, which are:

- necessity;
- impossibility;
- and possibility.

Necessity is that the intellect judges a thing to be established in such a way that its removal is not admissible. Impossibility is that the intellect judges a thing to be negated in such a way that its being established is not admissible. Possibility is that the intellect judges the two alternatives to be on an equal footing, in such a way that both the negation of it and the affirmation of it are admissible. And in the field of God's attributes, glorified and exalted is He, the judgements of the intellect are likewise three. The first kind of attribute is that which the intellect makes necessary for God; under this fall the attributes already mentioned, which the sound intellect makes necessary and to which sound transmitted evidence points …

flags.context: the record breaks off and the full text sits behind a download
options: render with an excerpt banner and link the .doc
flags.note: Excerpt only, style guide section 9. It breaks off on an ellipsis at the end of the first of the three kinds, so that the second and third kinds — the impossible and the possible — are defined in the abstract but never applied to God's attributes, although one of them is named in the title. The complete text sits behind /medias/doc/L-29.doc. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends and completes nothing. Must not be rendered as a whole lesson.

flags.arabic: الفقرة الافتتاحية مقابل ما بعد العنوان الفرعي
flags.context: the synopsis paragraph against the transcribed opening of the lesson
options: mark the synopsis as the site's own and the remainder as the Sheikh's words
present the whole record as the Sheikh's words
flags.note: The record has two authors. The first paragraph is a synopsis written by the site — it speaks about the lesson and its subject in the third person and does not begin with the opening formula. Everything from the section heading onward is transcribed speech in the Sheikh's own voice. The site must not present the synopsis as his words.

flags.arabic: الوجوب / الاستحالة / الجواز — مستحيلة وواجبة وجائزة
flags.context: the whole record: the three divisions of the rational judgement as applied to God's attributes
options: necessity / impossibility / possibility, as terms of rational modality
obligation / prohibition / permissibility, as legal rulings
flags.note: THE kalām exemption case in this slice, and the single highest-risk record in it. Style guide section 8 is decisive: 'واجب', 'جائز' and 'ممتنع/مستحيل' predicated of God's attributes are terms of rational modality, not the five legal rulings. Applying the five-rulings table here would produce the statement that certain of God's attributes are 'obligatory' and others 'permissible', which is not merely wrong but close to blasphemous in English. The record itself makes the point explicit — the subject is 'الحكم العقلي', the judgement of the intellect, not 'الحكم الشرعي' — and the definitions given are unmistakably modal: necessity is what the intellect cannot admit the removal of. Rendered throughout as necessity, impossibility and possibility. A reviewer should check this record first.

flags.context: the closing words of the site's synopsis
options: what follows from it in the science of theology (kalām)
the discussion that follows from it
what is consequent upon it in speech
flags.note: 'الكلام' with the definite article, in a passage about the divisions of the rational judgement, is the discipline of speculative theology, not 'speech' or 'discussion' in general. The reading is not certain — the plainer sense would be 'the discussion that follows from it' — so the Arabic is given in brackets and the alternative recorded.

flags.context: the first half of the title
flags.note: The title announces two subjects and the served text reaches neither by name. The first, 'faith before knowledge', is a recognised question in kalām — whether assent may or must precede demonstrative knowledge — but the excerpt contains nothing on it, so the English title has been kept as flat and uncommitted as the Arabic, and no position has been read into it.

flags.context: the last clause before the text breaks off
options: and to which sound transmitted evidence points
and which the authentic reports establish
flags.note: 'النقل' is the transmitted source — revelation and report — standing against 'العقل', the intellect, in the sentence's own pairing. 'صحيح' here qualifies transmission, so 'sound' rather than 'valid'. The clause matters: it states that for this first kind the intellect and transmission agree, and the agreement is the point being made when the text breaks off.

translator_notes: One of a run of fifteen records, IDs 707-721, in the written-creed section, all uploaded on 9 and 10 May 2011 within a few hours of one another, all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and the first lines of a lesson, and then breaks off on an ellipsis; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/L-* series, numbered L-26 to L-39 in the same order as the IDs. The uniform timestamps are a bulk upload and say nothing about when the lesson was delivered.

The record contains two distinct voices and the English keeps them apart. The opening paragraph is a synopsis written by the site, about the lesson and in the third person; everything from the section heading onward is the Sheikh's own words as transcribed. Nothing in the synopsis may be quoted as his.

The source's final line, 'تحميل المادة' ('download the material'), is the label of a download link in the page furniture, not part of the text. It is recorded as source_download_link and omitted from body_ar and body_en.
Style guide section 8 governs this record from beginning to end. Nothing in it is a legal ruling and nothing in it should be read through the five-rulings table.
The English sets the three divisions as a list where the source marks them with dashes on one line, which is how the source itself presents them. No word has been added.
'الأسماء الحسنى والصفات العلا' is rendered 'the most beautiful names and the most exalted attributes', keeping both superlatives as the Arabic has them.
